title: Natasha James vs Avinash Simon on 7 May, 2022

paragraphs.text:
HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD, LUCKNOW BENCH
 
 

?Court No. - 20
 

 
Case :- TRANSFER APPLICATION (CIVIL) No. - 183 of 2019
 

 
Applicant :- Natasha James
 
Opposite Party :- Avinash Simon
 
Counsel for Applicant :- Prashant Singh Gaur,Amitabh Pratap Singh
 
Counsel for Opposite Party :- Pankaj Singh,Pooja Bhargava Singh
 

 
Hon'ble Jaspreet Singh,J.
Heard Sri A.P.Singh, learned counsel for the petitioner.
None has put in appearance on behalf of the respondent though the names of Sri Pankaj Singh and Ms. Pooja Bhargava Singh, Advocates are printed in the cause list as counsel for the respondent.

The instant petition has been preferred by the petitioner under section 24 C.P.C. seeking transfer of the divorce suit bearing no. 2253 of 2017 (Avinash Simon Vs. Natasha James) under section 10 of the Indian Divorce Act, 1869, pending in the court of Principal Judge, Family Court, Lucknow to the appropriate court in distict-Meerut.

Initially, the transfer petition was filed on 09-12-2019 alongwith an affidavit of one Ms. Priyanka Spring and it was stated that she was a relative(cousin) of the petitioner. Notice was issued to the respondent, which was duly served, however, no Counter Affidavit has been filed as yet.

On 27-04-2022, the court noticing the affidavit filed in support of the petition by Ms. Priyanka Spring, had called upon the learned counsel for the petitioner to explain the maintainability of the petition. In the meantime, learned counsel for the petitioner has filed a Supplementary Affidavit reiterating the contents of the transfer application alongwith an affidavit of the petitioner, Natasha James.

It is submitted on behalf of the petitioner that any anomaly or defect in filing the aforesaid petition, which might have occurred in view of the affidavit filed by Ms. Priyanaka Spring on behalf of the petitioner would stand cured as the petitioner herself has filed her affidavit reiterating the contents and the same may be considered by the court for the purposes of transfer application.

Since, the matter is engaging attention of this court since the year 2019, as a result proceedings filed before the Principal Judge, Family Court at Lucknow are held up. Accordingly, instead of entering into the technicalities, the court accepts the affidavit filed by the petitioner in support of the transfer application and proposes to decide the same on merits.
The contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner is that petitioner and the respondent were married at Lucknow on 12-11-2015 as per the Christian rites.

It is further urged that soon after the marriage, the respondent and his family members started troubling the petitioner for want of adequate dowry. This compelled the petitioner to institute a complaint case No. 1131 of 2016 before the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, IIIrd at Meerut, which was withdrawn by the petitioner as the respondent had apologized and agreed not to cause any matrimonial discord.

Soon after withdrawal of the complaint case, the acts of the demand of dowry and harassing the petitioner continued once again as a result, the petitioner had to leave her matrimonial home and she is residing with her parents in district-Meerut.

At this stage, the petitioner also filed an F.I.R. against the respondent bearing Case Crime No. 437 of 2017 at Police Station-Sadar Bazar, district-Meerut. The petitioner also instituted a petition under section 12 of the Domestic Violence Act,2005 bearing Case No. 799 of 2017.
It is in the aforesaid backdrop that the respondent has instituted a petition for divorce bearing case no. 2253 of 2017 before the Family Court at Lucknow.

Further submission of learned counsel for the petitioner is that the father and mother of the petitioner have expired. Since prior to the death of the mother of the petitioner, who suffered from renal failure, the petitioner had to spend a large amount of money and she was not even in a position to contest the proceedings at district-Lucknow and now after having lost both the parents and being in a financial distress, the petitioner has taken up a job in a private school to maintain herself apart from the fact that no amount of maintenance has been awarded in the petition preferred by the petitioner under section 12 of the Domestic Violence Act nor the respondent has appeared in the said case.

In the aforesaid circumstances, where the petitioner is distraught and having no support system, in the aforesaid circumstances, it is prayed that the pending proceedings at Lucknow may be transferred to the Principal Judge, Family Court at Meerut, where already the petition under the D.V. Act is pending.

As already noticed above, as none has put in appearance nor any objections have been filed on behalf of the respondent, accordingly, considering the averments made in the petition and the affidavit filed by the petitioner,Natasha James and also noticing the dictum of the Apex Court in the case of Leena Mukherjee Vs. Rabi Shankar Mukherjee reported in 2002 (10 SCC 480, in the case of Pratibha Khemka Vs. Sanjay Kumar Khemka reported in 2004 (13) SCC 686 and in the case of Neelam Kanwar Vs. Devinder Singh Kanwar reported in 2000 (1) SCC 589, this court is of the opinion that ends of justice can be met by transferring the Case No. 2253 of 2017 from the court of Principal Judge, Family Court, Lucknow to the Principal Judge, Family Court at Meerut.

The Principal Judge, Family Court, Lucknow shall forthwith transmit the record of Case No. 2253 of 2017 to the transferee court at Meerut, who on receipt of the record and copy of the order passed by this court, after affording full opportunity of hearing to the parties, but, not granting any unnecessary adjournment, shall make an endeavour to decide the proceedings finally preferably within a period of one year from date of receipt of the record and copy of this order passed by this court.
With the aforesaid, the petition is allowed.
In the facts and circumstances of the case, there shall be no order as to costs.

Order Date :- 7.5.2022
 
AKS
